hook: SCP-870 is a predatory species that only people with schizophrenia can perceive, which means sightings usually get dismissed as hallucinations. The file is short, and most of its weight sits in a brief interview with a man who started following the creatures to prove to himself they were real. Read the researcher's closing note slowly.
whyItMatters: The premise turns a familiar horror question, whether the thing someone sees is really there, into a containment problem. Because no ordinary staff member can see the specimen, the procedures depend on a D-class with schizophrenia watching a camera feed around the clock. It is a compact example of an anomaly defined less by its body than by who is able to notice it.
thingsToNotice:
No two observers agree on its appearance: a three-eyed alligator on spider legs, a smoke figure shaped like a man, a hunched child topped with a parrot's head, a giant centipede that has human arms for legs. That inconsistency, plus the theory that it may not need food at all and instead turns victims into young over a long time, keeps the creature unknowable even in custody, where it bangs on its walls at all hours.

The interview finds horror in an everyday habit. The man watched one of them watching a neighbor, saw it snatch a ruler the neighbor dropped under his desk and eat it whole, and days later saw it swallow the neighbor too. Afterward he is amnesticized and released, and the closing statement worries that he has placed the species in a major population center.

The addendum then removes any comfort. The researcher suspects people with schizophrenia see only a little more of the creature than everyone else, and that the rest of us miss it because its camouflage is simply perfect.
